v: This directory is the full published CodeArchitect workspace for deployment, demos, and packaging: it bundles legal/privacy notices, benchmark harnesses and scripts, a Vite/React client, the MCP server implementation and public portal, packaged MCP microservices (codearchitect-mcp and sqlharness), and the Express-based backend that ingests, chunks, caches and serves project contexts for RAG/LLM flows. Its role is to provide everything needed to run, demo, benchmark, and distribute the MCP-backed CodeArchitect service (including safety/privacy docs, tooling for warmed summaries and previews, and reusable packaged components).

A privacy policy-like document that describes how different deployment modes handle source code, user data, caching, and model/provider retention: it distinguishes the hosted web demo, a local loopback server, and an independent MCP entry point, and lists what is and isn't persisted or shared in each case. Its role is to communicate privacy boundaries and operational constraints for those deployment options (what is stored, sent to providers, and what operators should avoid).

A brief third-party notices file that clarifies the project's MIT license applies only to original work by Andrew Jorge and does not relicense third-party data, dependencies, or trademarks. It specifically references the BigCode CommitPackFT/OctoPack dataset and warns to preserve upstream license metadata, provenance, and notices for included source examples, tree-sitter grammars, and npm dependencies.

Contains the benchmark harness and example configuration for measuring how CodeArchitect’s meaning cache affects question-answer latency; README explains what is measured, how to run dry/full benchmarks, configure trials, interpret telemetry and output files, while context.example.json provides a sample trial and question tasks to drive automated benchmark runs.

This README documents a benchmark harness that measures how CodeArchitect's meaning cache affects question-answer latency by comparing cold, prewarmed, and repeat states; it explains what is measured, how to run a dry validation and full benchmark, how to configure questions and repositories, and how to interpret the telemetry output. It also notes implementation details (temporary MEANING_CACHE_DIR, no changes to normal server responses), output files produced, and cautionary guidance about trial counts and what the metrics represent.

This JSON defines a test/configuration specifying one trial against a repository named "CodeArchitect" (path "..") and lists three question tasks; each task gives an id, target file path, a string to find in that file, and a natural-language question about that code. It’s used to drive automated queries or checks that locate the given export/function in the specified files and ask the listed developer-facing questions.

Frontend client for CodeArchitect: a Vite/React app (index.html, package.json, vite.config.js) whose src folder implements the UI, reusable components, styles, and utilities for browsing, viewing, editing and uploading project files. It mounts the top-level App at /src/main.jsx and uses the Vite dev server with an /api proxy to the Express backend for network requests.

An HTML document that serves as the app entry page for "CodeArchitect": it sets charset and viewport metadata, preloads Google fonts and a favicon, provides a root <div id="root"> for mounting the application, and loads the client JavaScript module /src/main.jsx.

This package.json defines a Node.js/JavaScript project named "client", marking it as an ES module project and listing metadata (version, private). It declares dev and build scripts using Vite, and specifies React and React DOM as runtime dependencies plus Vite and the React plugin as devDependencies for building and serving a React app.

Contains the full frontend application for the code-inspection workspace: a React entry (main.jsx) that mounts the top-level App component, a comprehensive set of reusable UI components for browsing, viewing, editing and managing projects, and a global stylesheet that defines the app’s design system and responsive behaviors. The lib utilities support networking, error handling, rich-text rendering, source-range helpers and folder upload prep so the UI can fetch, display, edit, and upload project files robustly.

This file defines a React component (default export App) that implements the top-level workspace UI for a code-inspection app: it manages project and file state, startup/health checks, project upload/switch/remove flows, chunk-size and edit persistence, various modals (privacy, licenses, caching, demo), and renders the Explorer, CodeViewer, and status/controls. It also includes two small presentational subcomponents (ProjectOverview and EmptyWorkspace) used when no file or project is selected.

Reusable React UI components for the code browsing and project management surface: an interactive chunked code viewer with diffing and editing helpers (CodeViewer), a file-context picker (ContextAttach), an accessible tab bar (InsightTabbar), a folder/file explorer with per-folder chat and navigation (Library), and a top-bar project switcher with upload/drag-drop and tab management (ProjectSwitcher). These components implement the app’s primary file navigation, context attachment, project switching, and in-place code inspection/editing interactions.

CodeViewer.jsx is a comprehensive React component that loads and renders a file's source text as an interactive, chunked code viewer with line-aware rendering, visual diffing (LCS-based char diffs), and per-line colored segments. It manages complex UI state and interactions — selection and highlights, chunk fetching and modes, edit drafts with history, scrolling/jump behavior, symbol lookups, and an integrated Q&A/chat/suggestion flow — and provides helper utilities for mapping DOM selections to absolute offsets and visual effects for focusing lines.

A React component that lets the user attach a single project file as "context": it renders a paperclip button that opens a searchable popover of the provided files and calls onChange(fileId) when a file is picked (or onChange(null) to remove). If value matches a file it instead shows a chip with the file name and a remove button; it also limits visible rows, supports incremental filtering by typing, and closes the popover on outside clicks.

A React functional component that renders an accessible tab bar titled by `label`, mapping `tabs` into tab buttons, highlights the `activeTab`, and calls `onTabChange(id)` when a tab is clicked. It optionally renders `leading` content at the start and an optional close button that invokes `onClose`. The component accepts a `className` prop to extend styling.

This file defines a React component "Library" that renders a project file explorer with filterable tree navigation, breadcrumb/back/forward folder navigation, file selection, and a folder-scoped chat UI that can send queries to askFolder and display clickable file/folder references. It includes helper functions to build/flatten a nested folder tree, render ASCII-style guide lines for the tree, detect referenced project items in assistant text, and manage per-folder chat state, edits annotation, and context file attachment.

A React component (forwardRef) that renders a top-bar project switcher: it displays open project tabs (with drag-to-reorder and remove for the active tab), a "+" chooser to pick/upload a folder (via File System Access API, input webkitdirectory fallback, or drag-and-drop), and a context settings popover with a bare-window slider and clear-cache action. It manages upload lifecycle (reading/uploading, preview, errors), maintains fixed tab ordering and drag/drop insertion indicator, and exposes an imperative openFolder method via ref.

A comprehensive CSS stylesheet that defines design tokens, global resets, themes, and detailed component styles for a complex web app UI—covering the app shell, topbar, project tabs, explorer/library, code viewer and panes (edit/history/chat/insight), toolbars, drawers, controls (sliders, switches, inputs), and many interactive states, animations and responsive behaviors. Its role is to unify colors, spacing, neumorphic/recessed surface treatments, accessibility preferences (reduced motion, scrollbar/autofill handling), and polished visuals (clip-paths, layered pseudo-elements, transitions) so all workspace, viewer, and panel components render consistently across breakpoints.

Client-side utility modules used by the app’s UI: a thin fetch-based API client that manages per-tab sessions, error-humanizing helpers, a rich-text-to-React renderer with mention handling, a source-range/line-number helper, and a folder-upload walker that prepares and filters files for server ingest. Together these provide networking, user-friendly errors, content rendering, source-location utils, and file-reading/upload shaping for the frontend.

A thin browser client module that wraps HTTP calls to an Express-based API, exporting async functions for health, file/project management, chunking, and RAG Q&A/editing endpoints. It centrally manages a per-tab session identifier (X-CodeArchitect-Session) via sessionStorage with a fallback and uses fetch to POST/GET/DELETE to the server, throwing on non-OK responses and returning parsed JSON/text.

Exports a function humanizeError that takes an error (or string) and returns a user-friendly error message: it extracts error.message if needed, returns a fallback when empty, and maps known error patterns (API key, network/unreachable, removed uploads, file chunk/load failures) to clearer, actionable text. If no pattern matches it returns the original message.

Parses a Markdown-like rich-text string (handling fenced ```code``` blocks, headings, **bold**, inline `code`, and preserving newlines) and returns an array of React elements representing that content. It also recognizes "mentions" (file/folder names) and turns whole-word occurrences or inline code into clickable <button> refs using provided mention handlers or a linkCode callback. The module's functions split and format prose, inline spans, and code blocks to render styled, interactive chat content.

Computes a 1-based line number for a byte offset in a string and uses that to produce a human-readable label for a half-open source range: "Line N" if the range stays on one line or "Lines A–B" if it spans multiple lines. It clamps start/end to valid bounds, treats ranges as [start,end), and uses end-1 when computing the last included line so a range that begins at the next line's start doesn't claim that line.

This module reads a user-selected folder (via <input webkitdirectory>, the File System Access API, or drag-and-drop entries), walks the tree, filters out unwanted directories/files and non-source or oversized files, and returns the upload-ready shape { name, files: [{ relPath, content }], truncated } while enforcing per-file, file-count, and total-byte caps. It mirrors server ingest filters (skip lists and source extensions), reads file text content, and marks the result truncated if caps are hit.

This module is the application entry point that imports React's createRoot, global CSS, and the top-level App component, then mounts the App into the DOM element with id "root" by creating a React root and rendering <App /> into it.

Vite configuration that enables the React plugin, runs the dev server on port 5174, and proxies requests starting with /api to an Express server at http://localhost:8799; it leaves changeOrigin false and explicitly sets the proxied request's Host header to the original incoming request's Host.

Contains the implementation and supporting utilities for a Model Context Protocol (MCP)-based "CodeArchitect" service: server code to run the MCP server and CLI/HTTP entrypoints (server.js), an Express router exposing demo and MCP/SQL proxy endpoints (public.js), safe file-reading and summarization tools that produce bounded parse-tree overviews (tools.js), and a pure selection/context extractor with guidance rules (focus.js). The demo directory shows a tiny billing/report example; overall this directory provides the context-generation, safety checks, and HTTP glue needed to serve structured code-selection contexts to downstream MCP clients.

Contains a small demo set of billing/report utilities: billing.js computes the total amount of orders with status "paid", and report.js wraps that function to produce a simple report object with a revenue field. This directory demonstrates a minimal flow from computing paid-order totals to building a revenue report.

Exports a function paidTotal that takes an array of order objects, filters for orders whose status is 'paid', and returns the sum of their amount fields. It computes the total monetary value of paid orders.

This module imports a function named paidTotal from './billing.js' and exports a function buildReport that takes an orders argument and returns an object with a single property revenue set to the result of calling paidTotal(orders). It therefore acts as a thin wrapper that builds a simple report object containing total paid revenue.

Exports ANSWER_GUIDANCE (a list of response rules) and a pure function selectionContext that, given file text, an AST and a selection (with line/column bounds), computes a bounded, structured context for that selection: it maps lines to offsets, validates the selection, finds the tightest AST nodes covering the highlight (preserving multiple top-level nodes if needed), and extracts truncated source excerpts for the highlight, focused nodes, ancestors, sibling outline entries and imports. It also returns a SHA-256 file fingerprint, budget metadata (characters used/omitted), guidance and limitations — all without performing I/O or external model calls.

This module exports createPublicRouter, a function that builds an Express router to serve a small public UI (static assets and HTML pages), a health endpoint, and two MCP server endpoints with host/origin checks, CORS headers, JSON body parsing and simple concurrency/size limits. One endpoint (/codearchitect/server) runs a local Model Context Protocol server instance using a StreamableHTTPServerTransport, while the other (/sqlharness/server) forwards sanitized protocol headers and the JSON body to a configured upstream SQL harness with timeout and response-size protection.

This file defines and exports functions to create and run a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server named "CodeArchitect": createServer registers a get_question_context tool (with input validation and result-size/error handling) and a privacy-policy resource, while main parses CLI options to either connect the server to stdio or start an express-based loopback HTTP demo endpoint that proxies MCP requests. It also contains a self-execution guard to run main when invoked directly and enforces port/origin validation and safety checks (e.g., disallowing HTTP demo access to arbitrary project roots).

Defines utilities for reading and summarizing source files under a constrained project root and exposes createTools, which returns a get_question_context method that either returns a parse-tree-backed selection context for a specific file range or an overview of top-level code units across files. It enforces safe access (allowed extensions, realpath checks, no symlinks, file size limits), parses files to trees, and builds a bounded structural overview (with budgeting and omission counts) suitable for feeding into later focus/answer guidance.

Contains the static web frontend for demoing and installing MCP-backed tools: shared assets (portal.css, portal.js) implementing the portal UI/behavior and two demo pages (codearchitect.html and sqlharness.html) that wire those assets into interactive example workspaces, show connection/endpoint details for the Streamable HTTP MCP server, and provide installation/local usage instructions and links.

Holds the frontend assets for a web portal demo: portal.css provides global styles, layout, responsive and accessibility rules, while portal.js implements the demo UI behavior (example prompts, backend JSON-RPC calls including event-stream parsing, rendering of structured results, endpoint selection, and UI helpers like clipboard and raw-output toggling). Together they define the portal’s appearance and client-side interaction with the backend.

This CSS file defines the visual design and layout for a web portal, including root color variables, typography, global resets, and component styles for the header, hero, workspace (prompts/result panes), buttons, forms, and footer. It also includes interactive states (hover/focus), responsive adjustments for small screens, and an accessibility rule for reduced motion.

This script powers a demo UI that lists preconfigured example prompts, calls a backend JSON-RPC endpoint to run selected example "tools", and renders the returned structured results into HTML (with custom render paths for projects codearchitect, sqlharness, and orcview). It handles endpoint selection, RPC (including text/event-stream parsing), response/error handling, dynamic example buttons, raw-output toggling, and a clipboard-copy helper.

An HTML document that provides a demo and installation UI for the "CodeArchitect MCP" tool: it loads styling and a script, declares the demo workspace (example prompts, result area), connection details (Streamable HTTP endpoint and example config), and local install instructions (npx command and download link). The page embeds metadata, copy buttons, and links to source and privacy info, and exposes the server endpoint via data attributes on the body for the included portal.js to use.

An HTML document that implements the static web UI for the "SQLHarness MCP" demo site: it presents a hero/introduction, an interactive demo area for example prompts and results, configuration/endpoint details for connecting the Streamable HTTP MCP server, and installation/local usage instructions and links. The page wires in external CSS/JS assets (/mcp/assets/portal.css and portal.js), exposes the demo server endpoint and copy buttons, and documents how to add the tool to VS Code or run it locally.

Contains two packaged MCP microservices and their tooling: codearchitect-mcp (a Node.js Model Context Protocol service with file access/parsing, selection/context extraction, guidance rules, ingestion/chunking, caching, demo flows and a CLI/server entrypoint) and sqlharness (a minimal, MCP-packaged SQLite-focused toolkit and microservice for dataset loading, validation/introspection, safe read-only execution and demo DB helpers). Together they provide reusable, safely packaged components for context extraction, code/SQL parsing and safe SQL testing/execution, ready for deployment and integration.

Contains the Node.js implementation and packaging for a Model Context Protocol (MCP) service: mcp/ provides safe file-access and parsing utilities, selection/context extraction and guidance rules, a demo billing/report flow, and an MCP server exposing a get_question_context tool (with CLI entrypoint). The server/ directory implements source ingestion, file discovery and chunking, lightweight language parsing (web-tree-sitter) with memoized in-memory and SHA1-keyed on-disk caching and cache tools; package.json describes the package, runtime deps, and included files.

Houses the MCP (Model Context Protocol) implementation and supporting utilities: safe file-access and parsing tools (tools.js) that build bounded structural overviews, a pure selection/context extractor and guidance rules (focus.js), a server that exposes a get_question_context tool and demo HTTP/stdio adapters (server.js), plus a small demo of billing/report utilities (demo/) to exercise the flow. Together these files provide secure project-scoped tooling for producing compact, fingerprinted selection contexts and an MCP server exposing that functionality.

Contains a small demo set of billing/report utilities: billing.js computes the total amount of orders with status "paid", and report.js wraps that function to produce a simple report object with a revenue field. This directory demonstrates a minimal flow from computing paid-order totals to building a revenue report.

Exports a function paidTotal that takes an array of order objects, filters for orders whose status is 'paid', and returns the sum of their amount fields. It computes the total monetary value of paid orders.

This module imports a function named paidTotal from './billing.js' and exports a function buildReport that takes an orders argument and returns an object with a single property revenue set to the result of calling paidTotal(orders). It therefore acts as a thin wrapper that builds a simple report object containing total paid revenue.

Exports ANSWER_GUIDANCE (a list of response rules) and a pure function selectionContext that, given file text, an AST and a selection (with line/column bounds), computes a bounded, structured context for that selection: it maps lines to offsets, validates the selection, finds the tightest AST nodes covering the highlight (preserving multiple top-level nodes if needed), and extracts truncated source excerpts for the highlight, focused nodes, ancestors, sibling outline entries and imports. It also returns a SHA-256 file fingerprint, budget metadata (characters used/omitted), guidance and limitations — all without performing I/O or external model calls.

This file defines and exports functions to create and run a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server named "CodeArchitect": createServer registers a get_question_context tool (with input validation and result-size/error handling) and a privacy-policy resource, while main parses CLI options to either connect the server to stdio or start an express-based loopback HTTP demo endpoint that proxies MCP requests. It also contains a self-execution guard to run main when invoked directly and enforces port/origin validation and safety checks (e.g., disallowing HTTP demo access to arbitrary project roots).

Defines utilities for reading and summarizing source files under a constrained project root and exposes createTools, which returns a get_question_context method that either returns a parse-tree-backed selection context for a specific file range or an overview of top-level code units across files. It enforces safe access (allowed extensions, realpath checks, no symlinks, file size limits), parses files to trees, and builds a bounded structural overview (with budgeting and omission counts) suitable for feeding into later focus/answer guidance.

This package.json defines a Node.js ES module package named "codearchitect-mcp" (v0.2.0) with metadata (description, MIT license), requires Node >=20, declares a CLI entrypoint "codearchitect-mcp" pointing to mcp/server.js, includes the mcp and server/ingest directories in the published files, and lists runtime dependencies (Model Context Protocol SDK, zod, tree-sitter-wasms, web-tree-sitter).

Contains server-side ingestion utilities for reading and prepping source code: discovering project files (respecting git/ignores and size limits), splitting files into labeled line-based chunks for viewer/editor use, and producing minimal language-agnostic parse trees via web-tree-sitter. It also manages parser runtime and grammar WASM loading with memoized in-memory and SHA1-keyed on-disk caching (plus cache-clear tools) and graceful handling when grammars are absent.

Holds utilities for ingesting source code: discovering and reading project files (respecting git, ignores, and size limits), splitting file text into labeled line-based chunks for viewer/editor use, and producing minimal language-agnostic parse trees via web-tree-sitter. It also manages parser runtime and grammar WASM loading, with memoized in-memory and on-disk (SHA1-keyed) caching and cache-clear utilities, plus graceful handling when grammars are missing.

Provides utilities to recursively discover source files in a project (respecting Git-tracked files when available, skipping configured directories/files and size limits), read a source file, determine a file's language by extension, and split file text into line-based "chunks" of non-empty lines (producing per-chunk line ranges, char offsets, labels, and counts) for use by a viewer/editor.

This module wraps web-tree-sitter to parse source text into a minimal, language-agnostic parse tree ({type, start, end, named, children}) using character offsets and including only named nodes, and it exposes parseToTree/loadTree with memoized in-memory and on-disk (SHA1-keyed) caching plus cache-clearing utilities. It also handles loading language WASM grammars (preferring local copies), initialization of the parser runtime, and graceful failures when a grammar is unavailable.

Holds a minimal MCP-packaged distribution of Andrew Jorge’s SQLHarness: a small SQLite-focused toolkit (types, dataset loaders, validation/introspection, read-only execution with safety limits and receipts) plus an MCP microservice exposing list/inspect/validate/explain/execute endpoints and demo DB helpers. It includes packaging (pyproject, console entrypoint) and license/third-party notices documenting dependencies and included MIT-licensed fixtures, intended for safe SQL testing/benchmarking without model or credential dependencies.

This README documents a minimal MCP distribution of Andrew Jorge's SQLHarness, explaining that it reuses Python database authority, SQLGlot validation, and bounded read-only execution while omitting research/model-generation dependencies. It notes that sample data are exposed via a public CodeArchitect page, a local database root is available over stdio only, and no model calls or credentials are required.

This file documents licensing and third-party component scope for the project: it states that the original authority code and a synthetic shop fixture are MIT-licensed (attributed to Andrew Jorge), that the MCP SDK and SQLGlot dependencies keep their upstream licenses, and that no BIRD database is bundled.

This pyproject.toml configures packaging and build for the project: it specifies Hatchling as the build backend, project metadata (name, version, license, description, Python requirement), runtime dependencies (mcp and sqlglot), a console script entry point (sqlharness-mcp -> sqlharness.mcp_server:main), and a wheel build target that includes the src/sqlharness package.

Contains a small SQLite-focused testing, benchmarking and validation toolkit plus an MCP microservice: types and dataclasses for benchmark records, dataset loaders, SQL validation/introspection and read-only execution/result-comparison logic that enforce safety (timeouts, row limits, normalization) and produce stamped receipts and structured Execution/Validation results. The microservice exposes list/inspect/validate/explain/execute operations against a rooted set of SQLite databases and includes helpers to create a demo database and run the server.

Holds a small SQLite-focused testing and benchmarking toolkit: types and dataclasses for benchmark records, dataset loaders that match examples to database files, SQL validation/introspection utilities, read-only execution and result-comparison logic, and an authority-backed MCP microservice that exposes list/inspect/validate/explain/execute operations against a rooted set of SQLite databases. It enforces safe read-only execution (timeouts, row limits, normalization), produces stamped receipts and structured Execution/Validation results, and includes helpers to create a demo database and run the server.
This package initializer declares the package docstring and defines the exposed names: it sets __all__ to ["__version__"] and defines the package version string __version__ = "0.1.0".

Provides a DatabaseAuthority class that resolves SQLite database files under a configured root and offers operations to list databases, introspect schema, validate readonly SQL, execute readonly queries, and produce EXPLAIN plans. It enforces database-id validation and root containment, applies readonly/normalization validation, constrains execution with timeout and row limits, and returns stamped receipts (SHA-256-based ID) describing decisions and results.

Provides utilities for loading and validating a BIRD dataset file into a list of BirdExample objects (supports JSON or JSONL, enforces required fields, normalizes evidence and SQL), locating a matching SQLite database file under a root path, and introspecting/rendering the SQLite schema. It also includes small helpers for reading the JSON payload and validating required string fields.

Provides utilities for running read-only SQLite queries and comparing their results. execute_sqlite_readonly opens a read-only SQLite connection with time/size limits, runs a query, normalizes cell values (floats/bytes), and returns an ExecutionResult including rows, columns, latency, and truncated flag; results_equivalent compares two ExecutionResult objects for equivalence (optionally order-sensitive) and sql_requires_order detects whether a SQL string contains an ORDER clause using sqlglot. The private helper _normalize_cell canonicalizes floats (including NaN) and bytes for stable comparison.

This module builds and runs a constrained MCP (microservice) server that exposes read-only SQLite database operations: it defines a create_server function that registers tools (list_databases, inspect_schema, validate_sql, explain_sql, execute_readonly_sql) guarded by a DatabaseAuthority and a JSON privacy resource, plus a _bounded helper to enforce result-size and error handling. It also includes create_demo_database to materialize a synthetic "shop" SQLite DB and a main() CLI to run the server either with that demo data or a user-provided database root.

Defines a set of frozen dataclasses that model data used in an SQL-generation benchmarking pipeline: BirdExample (example metadata), TokenUsage (token counts), Generation (model output and usage), ValidationResult (SQL validation details), ExecutionResult (query execution outcome), and BenchmarkRecord (combined record linking example, generation, validation, and executions). The classes serve as immutable, typed containers for passing, storing, and serializing benchmarking data (BenchmarkRecord provides to_dict via dataclasses.asdict).

Parses and validates a single read-only SQL statement (using sqlglot) against a provided schema: it ensures the SQL is a single query (no DDL/DML/transaction/administrative statements), checks referenced tables and columns (handling CTEs and aliases), collects referenced tables/columns, normalizes the SQL, and returns a ValidationResult containing validity, normalized SQL, deduplicated errors, and referenced names.

Contains utility and developer scripts for benchmarking, local previewing, and preparing cached summaries: a CLI that runs end-to-end context benchmarks and writes JSON/Markdown reports, a small Express preview server for the public router, and a script that generates and exports warmed "bare" summaries for demo data.

A Node CLI script that runs end-to-end "context" benchmarks: it loads a JSON config of repositories and questions, registers and scans each project, runs configurable trials that warm and query a meaning/answer pipeline while collecting telemetry, compacts and summarizes timing/cache/model metrics, and writes JSON and Markdown reports. It handles argument parsing, temporary isolated cache setup (with a dry-run mode), computes percentiles and reductions, and records environment and git state for reproducible results.

Creates an Express application, mounts the router returned by createPublicRouter at the "/mcp" path with a configured sqlEndpoint, and starts an HTTP server listening on 127.0.0.1:9020 while logging a preview URL to the console.

This script loads the repository project files, builds a project tree, and triggers generation/warming of "bare" (basic) summaries for every file and folder using the project's LLM warm function. It then reads those cached summaries, verifies they're present, and writes them as newline-delimited JSON records to demo/basic-summaries.jsonl.

Server-side backend for the Code Viewer: it implements an Express HTTP/static server and project registry (store) that loads, caches and serves projects and files, controls parsing/chunking and cache invalidation, and exposes endpoints for chunking, reference search, and RAG-style LLM Q&A/edit-suggestion operations. Supporting modules handle source discovery/parsing into stable chunks (ingest/), the LLM-driven summarization/caching/orchestration subsystem (llm/), and runtime benchmarking/telemetry utilities (benchmark/) used for instrumentation and performance analysis.

Holds utilities for runtime benchmarking and observability: conditional span-based content tracing (start/log spans and trace events) and an AsyncLocalStorage-backed telemetry context that measures durations, timing buckets, cache access/set counts, and model call stats. These helpers let code run with telemetry, record measurements (or attach them to errors), and produce snapshots for performance analysis and instrumentation.

This module provides helpers for conditional content tracing: contentTraceEnabled() checks whether tracing is enabled via environment variables, traceStep(name, input, fn) wraps an async operation in a traced span and logs its input and (if present) output without changing behavior, and traceEvent(name, input, output) records a single span-based log entry for an event by starting a span, logging input/output, and ending it.

This module provides an AsyncLocalStorage-based telemetry context for timing and counting operations: it lets code run inside runWithTelemetry to collect durations, timing buckets, cache access/set counters, and model call statistics, and returns a snapshot of telemetry on completion (or attaches it to errors). It also exposes helpers (measureTelemetry, recordCacheAccess, recordCacheSet, recordModelCall, telemetryActive) to record timings and counters into the current telemetry context.

This file implements an Express-based HTTP API and static server for a "Code Viewer" service: it manages a project registry (local or uploaded), scans and serves source files and chunked/parsed representations, exposes endpoints for chunking, reference search, and RAG-style LLM Q&A/edit-suggestion operations, and controls cache/parse-tree invalidation and project warm-up. It also serves a built client when present and boots by loading a default project directory at startup.

Contains the pipeline and helpers for discovering and reading project source files, parsing them (via web-tree-sitter or generic/json fallbacks), converting parse trees into a compact "box" representation, and slicing those boxes into stable, cached, content-hashed chunks for viewer/editor consumption. It also includes project-tree hashing/lookup, reference-finding across files, and utilities to build and navigate per-file node maps used by the frontier/chunking engine.

Provides utilities to recursively discover source files in a project (respecting Git-tracked files when available, skipping configured directories/files and size limits), read a source file, determine a file's language by extension, and split file text into line-based "chunks" of non-empty lines (producing per-chunk line ranges, char offsets, labels, and counts) for use by a viewer/editor.

Converts a tree-sitter-like parse tree (nodes with type/start/end/children) into a lightweight "box" tree of only named structural nodes (dropping anonymous operators/punctuation as gaps), then uses cached frontier utilities to build and cut that box tree into chunks for the frontier engine. It exposes boxFromParse to produce the box representation and chunkCode which hashes the source, caches the built box tree, and calls cutTree to produce the final chunks.

This module implements a source-agnostic "box tree" chunking engine: it balances a hierarchical parse-tree, assigns stable IDs and content hashes to every node, and then slices that tree into contiguous flat chunks either to meet a requested granularity/depth-spread or to isolate the tightest box around a highlighted range. It also computes per-chunk character coverage (respecting left-/right-attaching delimiters), collects the minimal ancestor node map for emitted chunks, and caches built trees keyed by content.

Creates a hierarchical parse tree for arbitrary text by using indentation to form line nesting and by splitting leaf lines into bracketed groups and comma/semicolon-separated segments (while skipping // and /* */ comments). The module builds and finalizes nodes (container vs leaf) with labels and depths, and exports chunkGeneric which caches the built tree and passes it to the shared cutTree frontier function.

This module parses JSON (with // and /* */ comments tolerated) into a node tree with character-span offsets and then converts that parse tree into a "box tree" (objects split into key/value boxes, arrays into indexed boxes, scalars as leaves) suitable for downstream chunking. It exports parseJsonTree (the parser) and chunkJson (which caches a built box tree and hands it to the frontier/cutting helpers imported from frontier.js).

This module wraps web-tree-sitter to parse source text into a minimal, language-agnostic parse tree ({type, start, end, named, children}) using character offsets and including only named nodes, and it exposes parseToTree/loadTree with memoized in-memory and on-disk (SHA1-keyed) caching plus cache-clearing utilities. It also handles loading language WASM grammars (preferring local copies), initialization of the parser runtime, and graceful failures when a grammar is unavailable.

Builds a content-addressed project folder tree from a list of files (computing per-file and per-directory SHA‑1 hashes and “bare” keys), holds one active tree module‑level, and provides helpers to set/get that active tree and to return the chain of folder nodes from the project root down to a directory (or the directory containing a given file). The directory hash is computed bottom‑up as the hash of sorted child hashes, files use the hash of their content, and nodes are indexed by path in a Map for fast lookup.

Search-based "find references": given an identifier name and a list of files, this module scans each file (using a tree-sitter parse tree when available, otherwise a word-boundary regex) for exact identifier occurrences, classifies each hit as definition/call/import/reference/text based on node context, groups hits by file, bounds the total hits, and returns a structured result including definitions and per-file hit lists. It also maps byte offsets to 1-based line numbers and extracts a trimmed line preview for each hit.

Exports functions to build a complete id→node map for a file (matching the chunking logic for JSON, code via tree-sitter, or a generic fallback) and a set of utilities to navigate that flat node map: finding semantic parents, semantic paths, inverting to children, computing semantic children and max depth, collecting proper ancestors, and producing a minimal tiling ("frontier") that isolates a set of marked boxes. Its role is to provide a file-scoped, stateless representation of the box/tree structure and the core operations needed to resolve and manipulate nodeIds for UI/meaning recursion.

Holds the LLM-driven "meaning" subsystem: persistent and ephemeral caches plus the engine that builds, caches, and serves context-free and context-aware natural-language summaries, Q&A and edit-suggestion results for files and folders. Together these modules manage durable JSONL-backed and per-session in-memory caches (with invalidation, pruning, migration and telemetry) and orchestrate OpenAI calls (windowed map-reduce, concurrency/deduplication, folding across folder chains, clipping/splitting, and session frontiers) to provide packaged summary/answer/edit outputs.

This module implements a two-tier cache for "meanings": a durable, append-only JSONL-backed store of shared basic summaries (loaded into mem/kinds and persisted to FILE) and ephemeral in-memory per-session focused summaries (stored in focusedSessions, pruned by TTL and capped). It provides cacheGet/cacheSet, file-hash-based invalidation and pruning/clearing utilities, handles legacy-file migration, and records telemetry while tolerating disk failures by falling back to memory.

This module implements a comprehensive "meaning" engine for source code that builds and caches both context-free (bare) and context-aware (contextualized) natural-language summaries of files and folders, using OpenAI with windowed map-reduce, concurrency slots, in-flight deduplication, and telemetry/tracing. It also provides contextual folding across folder chains, per-session user marks and frontiers, and LLM-backed Q&A and edit-suggestion APIs for chunks, files, and folders, along with utilities for clipping/splitting text and eagerly warming project summaries; many operations return packaged results containing answer, summary, and path.

This module implements an in-memory project registry and active-project manager: it registers projects (from disk or uploaded entries), lazily loads and caches their source files with LRU eviction, enforces caps (file/byte limits), and exposes accessors for the active project's files, scan stats, and per-project settings like a "bare window" size. It also provides removal/listing, a built-in sample file fallback, and utilities for building file metadata (IDs, line counts) and scanning directories into the registry.
